subject: maths
title: Time and Measurement - Days, Length and Mass
introductionText:
Term 2 · Measure
Time and Measurement — Days, Length
and Mass
The Big Idea: A week has 7 days and a year has 12 months. We measure length by
counting same-size cubes laid end to end, and compare mass with a balance: the heavier
side goes down.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"There are 7 days in a week: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday,
Saturday — then Sunday comes round again. There are 12 months in a year, starting with
January and ending with December. A balance is like a see-saw. When Daddy sits on one
end, that end goes down. The heavier thing always goes down."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
"Bigger means heavier." A big pillow is lighter than a small stone. Put them on a coat-
hanger balance and let the balance surprise him.
Leaving gaps when measuring. Cubes must touch, end to end, starting exactly at the end
of the object. A gap is a piece of length that nobody counted.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — The coat-hanger balance (10 minutes)
Hang a plastic bag on each end of a coat hanger and hang it from a door handle. Put an
apple in one bag and a potato in the other. He guesses which is heavier, then lets go and
watches. Then try three things — an onion, a spoon, a sock — and put them in order,
heaviest first.
Game 2 — How many bricks long? (10 minutes)
Use Lego bricks, dice or sugar cubes — all the same size. Measure a spoon, a book and his
shoe. He guesses first, then lines them up with no gaps. Then measure the same book
with your hand-spans and his. Why did we get different answers?
The heavier side goes DOWN
Measuring with cubes
big pillow
about 7 cubes long — no gaps!
small stone
Ask which object is heavier and how the balance shows it. Then count the cubes under the pencil with him.
More examples to talk about
• In Egypt the weekend is Friday and Saturday. Ask him which days he goes to school.
• February is the shortest month. His birthday is in one of the 12 months — which one?
• A balloon is big and very light; a key is small and heavy for its size.
• Tricky: hand-spans give different answers for different people. That's why we need
same-size units.
• To find the heaviest of three, compare two, then compare the winner with the third.
Key Words
day week month year measure cube length heavy heavier heaviest
light balance mass

A year has...
( 7 months ) ( 12 months ) ( 10 months )

On a balance, the heavier side goes...
( sideways ) ( down ) ( up )

When measuring with cubes, leave...
( big gaps ) ( no gaps ) ( one gap )

The day after Saturday is...
( Sunday ) ( Friday ) ( Monday )

( a strawberry ) ( a grape ) ( a watermelon )
